articleTitle: A Scientific Discovery in Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality Enriched with Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) powered Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) technologies enrich the user experience by providing innovative solutions in a wide range of fields such as education, healthcare, gaming, architecture and tourism. While VR provides users with an interactive experience in a fully digital universe, AR uses physical and virtual elements simultaneously by overlaying digital objects or information on the real world. Artificial intelligence algorithms make it possible for these environments to become more realistic, dynamic and personalized. In this bibliometric analysis study, scientific publications in the fields of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) were comprehensively analyzed. By revealing the citation densities, author profile analysis, and cross-country collaboration networks of 476 articles obtained from the Web of Science (WoS) database, the study demonstrated that the topic is a rapidly growing area in the academic literature that encourages interdisciplinary collaborations. VOSwiever (version 1.6.20), R studio (2024.12.1) Bibliometrix package and Gephi (0.10.1) were used for bibliometric analysis.

articleTitle: Evaluating Machine Learning Algorithms for Enhancing Network Intrusion Detection Systems: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) play crucial role for maintaining the security of modern network infrastructures. With the increasing sophistication of cyber-attacks, traditional signature-based methods have become insufficient. Machine Learning (ML) techniques offer a promising alternative, providing the ability to detect novel threats by learning from network traffic patterns. This article provides a comparative analysis of different ML algorithms applied to NIDS, evaluating their performance based on key metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and Fl-score.

articleTitle: Enhancing Online Laboratories' Security Through the Use of RFID Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) is a tech-nology that has been used to identify and track objects or individuals. It is used in inventory management for tracking and monitoring stock levels in real-time, in financial transactions, such as contactless payment systems, and in user authentication, by supporting access control systems to grant or restrict entry to secure areas, such as offices, laboratories, and restricted facilities. Additionally, RFID technology is used in transportation sys-tems for electronic toll collection, in healthcare for patient tracking and equipment monitoring, and also in personal devices for enabling smart home functionalities. Its flexibility, scalability, and reliability make RFID an indispensable tool in modern technological ecosystems. The proposed system addresses challenges faced by educational and research institutions in managing online laboratory resources, ensuring only authorized personnel can remotely access online laboratories, similar to what happens in physical laboratory facilities in which researchers and staff have to use their ID cards to gain access to laboratory facilities. This work uses an Online Laboratory Management System, where the laboratory users are assigned unique RFID tags, which serve as digital identifiers. Upon typing user and password credentials and scanning their RFID tags in a reader attached to their computers, the system will verify both authentication methods in real-time via a centralized database and grant or deny access accordingly. The proof of concept features a web-based interface for users and administrators to manage user roles and monitor access logs, Additionally, it provides access to a particular set of online laboratory stations based on the role validation. By leveraging RFID technology, any system can add an extra layer of security to traditional password-based authentication. With the use of this approach, it is expected to have a more secure system with the support of a flexible and configurable access control mechanism, contributing to the online laboratory user experience.

articleTitle: Development of Two-Stage Steganography Method
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: In the contemporary digital era, ensuring robust data security remains a critical challenge. Consequently, steganography, the practice of covertly embedding information, has attracted significant research interest. Steganography leverages modern technological advancements, including data compression techniques, information theory, cryptography, and spread spectrum technologies, to conceal sensitive information within various digital media, such as images, text documents, audio, and video files. This paper presents a novel two-stage text steganography approach utilizing the Least Significant Bit (LSB) method, specifically tailored for embedding confidential data within text documents. Initially, secret information is encoded into a DOCX document by subtly altering the color attributes of text characters, exploiting the minimal perceptibility of color changes by the human eye. Recognizing vulnerabilities inherent in the DOCX format structure, the second stage involves embedding this modified DOCX file within a PDF document, thereby enhancing concealment security through structural complexity. The proposed method significantly improves the robustness and imperceptibility of concealed information, effectively safeguarding it from unauthorized extraction attempts.

articleTitle: Debate-Driven Multi-Agent LLMs for Phishing Email Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Phishing attacks remain a critical cybersecurity threat. Attackers constantly refine their methods, making phishing emails harder to detect. Traditional detection methods, including rule-based systems and supervised machine learning models, either rely on predefined patterns like blacklists, which can be bypassed with slight modifications, or require large datasets for training and still can generate false positives and false negatives. In this work, we propose a multi-agent large language model (LLM) prompting technique that simulates debates among agents to detect whether the content presented on an email is phishing. Our approach uses two LLM agents to present arguments for or against the classification task, with a judge agent adjudicating the final verdict based on the quality of reasoning provided. This debate mechanism enables the models to critically analyze contextual cue and deceptive patterns in text, which leads to improved classification accuracy. The proposed framework is evaluated on multiple phishing email datasets and demonstrate that mixed -agent configurations consistently outperform homogeneous configurations. Results also show that the debate structure itself is sufficient to yield accurate decisions without extra prompting strategies.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Education Within the Scope of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy in Turkey
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This study examines AI-based education projects led by Turkey's Ministry of National Education. AI integration aims to enhance student achievement, optimize teaching, and support pedagogical practices. Intelligent tutoring systems, personalized learning platforms, and automated assessments provide individualized learning experiences, improving educational effectiveness. Under Turkey's 2021–2025 National AI Strategy, various initiatives focus on AI applications in teacher training, curriculum integration, and digital education platforms. Notably, the Education Informatics Network (in Turkish EBA) employs AI-powered recommendation systems to track student progress and address learning gaps. This study explores AI in education through teacher training, curriculum integration, student support, and data security. Findings suggest increasing AI adoption, yet ethical concerns, algorithmic bias, and data privacy remain critical challenges. Sustainable policy strategies are recommended to address these issues.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Task Scheduling in Fog-Cloud Environments: LS-NSGA-II Optimization and Blockchain Integration for Enhanced Security and Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Task scheduling in fog-cloud environments, particularly when managing complex resource allocations and task priorities, presents a significant challenge. This paper proposes a novel approach that integrates the hill climbing algorithm which is a well-known Local Search technique in the Non dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II, called LS- NSGA-II to address these issues. In fact, the LS-NSGA- II is used to optimize task assignments across nodes, aiming to minimize execution time while maximizing task priority. Simultaneously, ensures an immutable, transparent, and auditable record of all scheduling decisions, validating each task assignment against resource constraints to enhance system reliability and security. The approach begins by enhancing the reliability of the system initializing a population of candidate solutions, which are iteratively refined using a local search algorithm and then processed by NSGA-II to explore the pareto front of potential solutions. At each iteration, blockchain is employed to record and validate the most effective scheduling decisions, ensuring that only feasible and optimal solutions are preserved. Furthermore, blockchain facilitates audits, detects anomalies, and maintains system consistency by comparing the current state with previously recorded transactions. This mechanism provides an additional layer of security, safeguarding task scheduling against tampering and manipulation. This work establishes a foundation for future research into decentralized and secure task scheduling mechanisms in dynamic, distributed computing environments, with potential applications in edge computing, IoT, and beyond.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of DeepSeek-R1 Model in Transforming Healthcare Solutions: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Over the past few decades, artificial intelligence (AI) has become more integrated into healthcare, with Large Language Models (LLMs) being a key component in improving healthcare decision-making. These LLMs' capacity to produce and interpret human-like texts has the potential to revolutionize healthcare procedures, where efficient data processing and communication are crucial. DeepSeek-Rl, created by DeepSeek AI, has drawn notice globally for its reasoning-based design that uses reinforcement learning (RL) to enhance problem-solving skills. Keeping this in view, the paper emphasizes the significance of the DeepSeek- Rl model and its application in the healthcare industry. Highlighting some hypothetical potential scenarios, we believe that DeepSeek models can playa crucial role in transforming existing medical approaches and revolutionizing the future of AI in health care.

articleTitle: Investigating NoSQL Injection Attacks on MongoDB Web Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Modern web applications are increasingly data-intensive and handle a wide variety of semi-structured and unstructured data. Traditional relational databases were not designed to manage such data, and using them often leads to complications in storage, retrieval, and performance degradation. As a result, NoSQL databases have become more popular in recent years. With key advantages such as high performance, scalability, and support for diverse data structures, NoSQL databases are particularly well suited for handling large volumes of data, making them a popular choice for small businesses seeking efficient storage solutions. However, storing sensitive information in these databases makes them targets for attackers aiming to steal data or compromise applications. One of the major security threats to NoSQL databases is NoSQL injection, which attackers exploit to gain unauthorized access. This research investigates how MongoDB-based web applications can be exploited through simulated NoSQL injection attacks, examines their impact, and evaluates mitigation techniques to prevent these security risks. The findings aim to help NoSQL database developers understand the mechanisms of NoSQL injection attacks and implement stronger security measures to protect sensitive data.

articleTitle: Solving the Financial, Operational, and Reputational Impact of Commercial Fleet Collisions: Challenges and Mitigation Strategies Using Data-Driven Decision-Making Process
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This study discusses about collisions involving commercial fleet vehicles can have significant financial, operational, and reputational consequences for businesses. Beyond immediate vehicle damage, such incidents may lead to client loss and diminished sales due to compromised customer trust and service reliability. Operational expenses often increase from administrative burdens and legal processes, while insurance premiums may rise, further straining financial resources. Productivity can decline due to vehicle downtime, employee absences, and the need for staff replacements, contributing to higher payroll costs. Additionally, accelerated fleet equipment depreciation necessitates premature repairs or replacements. Accidents can also severely damage a company's reputation, resulting in negative publicity and long-term business setbacks. These multifaceted impacts underscore the importance of proactive risk management and safety measures to mitigate financial losses and preserve corporate reputation.

articleTitle: Advanced Forensic Analysis for Vehicle Speed Estimation: A Two-Video Comparison Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: A forensic analysis method for estimating vehicle speed is introduced by comparing two video sources from the same device (e.g., smartphone, security camera) in the same field of view. An initial reference video, featuring a single vehicle with a known speed determined by GPS data, is required for the proposed algorithm. Using this reference, the speed of a vehicle in a second video-where the speed is unknown or under question-can be estimated. Speed calculation in the second video relies on a user-defined region of interest (ROI), which is specified by free-hand drawing two lines. The algorithm combines the YOLO method and some optimization techniques in order to reduce processing time-by up to 97%. This approach offers a significant improvement in forensic video analysis, providing a faster and more reliable method for estimating vehicle speeds over a defined distance, which is crucial for law enforcement and investigations.

articleTitle: Recognizing the Financial Fraud Type of Telegram Advertisement Posts Based on the Multimodal Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: The instant messaging applications such as Tele-gram, Wire, and Signal have been widely used by cyber criminals for the fast propagation of illicit advertisements, particularly financial frauds. Examples of fraud include credit card scams, bank account drops, promo abuse/discount fraud, and money transfers. This paper explores the application of the multi- modal learning technique to analyze financial fraud activities on Telegram. We collected the data from 10 channels in the Telegram which including text and image. By combining text and image data, the multimodal learning especially the combination of Swin Transformer embeddings with attention-based fusion delivered the best results, which offers a more accurate approach to detecting financial frauds, capturing nuanced details that may be missed by single-modal learning methods. Integrating multiple data types allows for a higher accurate and Fl-score classification of fraud behavior, enhancing the capability to identify and prevent various types of frauds.

articleTitle: Muffins vs. Chihuahuas Revisited: Exploring Zero-Shot and Few-Shot CLIP-Based Methods for Similar Object Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Similar object classification represents an important problem in computer vision. While models based on convolutional neural networks (CNN) historically struggled to distinguish visually similar objects, advancements in Vision Transformers (ViT) and more recently in vision-language models like OpenAI's CLIP have reinvigorated interest in zero-shot and few-shot learning approaches. We explore methods that combine CLIP's zero-shot classification capabilities with a few-shot embedding comparison strategy. By balancing these two paradigms, a near-perfect accuracy was achieved for the similar object recognition benchmark problem muffins vs. chihuahuas. The quality of this approach is further validated on additional tasks, such as differentiating cats from dogs, achieving 99.35% accuracy. The presented results illustrate that the synergy of zero-shot and few-shot paradigms is highly effective in tackling similar object image classification challenges without specialized training.

articleTitle: Gaming Without Harm: AI-Driven Content Moderation to Improve Safety in Roblox
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Adolescents extensively use social media and gaming platforms, which are prone to exposure to inappropriate content. Despite existing chat moderation systems, such as Roblox's hashtag-based filters, users bypass them using altered expletive variations. This project proposes an enhanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) solution to improve content moderation by detecting expletive words, and their near-identical variations. Utilizing datasets from Carnegie Mellon University and GitHub, synthetic variations of expletives are generated using the Levenshtein Edit-Distance algorithm. Then, Jaro similarity measure is employed to identify subtle linguistic modifications on expletive content. The solution's accuracy is tested against Roblox's current filtering system, evaluating improvements in detecting inappropriate content. While Roblox's chat moderation system had a success rate of 44.6% when detecting expletive content, the proposed solution (ChatGuard) achieved 82.5% accuracy. Overall, the findings result in enhancing online safety and mitigate risks to adolescent users while balancing the need for effective moderation with freedom of expression.

articleTitle: From Snap to Evidence: Snapchat Footprint on iOS
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Snapchat has transformed how we communicate, especially for Gen Z, by offering a platform where moments disappear as quickly as they are shared. This ephemeral design promises users privacy and freedom from digital permanence. It also raises unique challenges for forensic investigations. In this study, we dive into the hidden layers of Snapchat's iOS application using various forensic techniques and tools. Our discovery challenges Snapchat's claims of complete data deletion. Media files, unsent snaps, and even detailed location data were found lingering in directories long after they were supposedly erased. These findings uncover potential hidden evidence valuable for forensic investigations, and raise serious questions about user privacy and the true nature of “ephemeral” messaging. By exposing the discrepancies between Snapchat's claims and its practices, our research also underscores the need for greater transparency from those social media platforms regarding their user information handling.

articleTitle: Detection of Dynamic Code Loading in Android
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Over the past decade, mobile phone usage has surged, with Android dominating the smartphone market. While its open ecosystem facilitates app development, it also makes Android devices a major target for malware attacks. Despite Google Play Protect scanning applications for malware, malicious apps that steal personal and financial data still infiltrate the Play Store. Play Protect struggles to detect advanced techniques like dynamic code loading (DCL) which enables malware to inject harmful code via updates, runtime downloads, or pre-packaged files. Recent research has revealed gaps in Google's policies that enable this behavior, making it a significant threat to Android security. However, previous works do not address this inability to detect DCL behavior or fail to create lightweight models suitable for resource-constrained mobile devices. This work aims to overcome these limitations by focusing on DCL behavior detection in Android malware while ensuring the model remains lightweight. The detection of DCL behavior is achieved by combining manifest-based and code-based features, which are characteristic of Android malware with DCL behavior. Through testing various combinations of features, we identified an optimal feature set of 32 features, which achieved comparable performance to the full feature set with an F1-score of 96 %. This allowed us to reduce the model size by selecting a minimal feature set, minimizing resource usage while maintaining high predictive performance.

articleTitle: Automated Static Analysis of Linux ELF Malware: Framework and Application
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: The rapid evolution of Linux malware, driven by an increased use of Linux in critical infrastructure, IoT, and cloud environments, underscores the need for scalable static analysis techniques for malware characterization and detection. This study presents an architecture-agnostic framework for static analysis, covering the entire pipeline from raw ELF binaries to machine learning-based focused studies. To facilitate large-scale ELF mal ware analysis, this study introduces elf radar, a static analysis feature extraction tool that leverages open-source binary analysis frameworks such as Radare2 and LIEF. In addition to extracting ELF meta-data and features pertinent to malware analysis, elfradar ex-tracts the Intermediate Representation (IR) of opcodes, enabling architecture-independent analysis for tasks such as opcode aggre-gated entropy-based assessments, and cross-architecture feature extraction. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, a dataset comprising approximately 20,000 ELF malware binaries from VirusShare was processed using elfradar. As a case study, outlier analysis was conducted on this dataset to identify potential indicators of obfuscation and packed samples. The efficacy of the proposed framework and static analysis feature extraction tool has been demonstrated in other studies as well, including Linux IoT malware variant classification, opcode entropy-based malware detection, and other applications focusing on static malware analysis.

articleTitle: MemLOL: Memory-Based LOLBins Dataset for Fileless Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Fileless malware has emerged as a prominent cyber threat that does malicious activities in memory to evade traditional detection methods. Fileless malware leaves very minimal forensic traces on disk. These attacks leverage LOLBins (Living Off the Land Binaries), legitimate system tools such as wscript.exe, dllhost, and powershell, wmic, etc, to perform the malicious operations, hence escape detection techniques. Fileless malware leads the threat rogue along deep fakes and ransomwares. Advanced detection techniques tailored to detect such sophisticated attack vectors are mandatory. Despite the growing threat, research in fileless malware detection lags due to the lack of publicly available datasets. The proposed work addresses this critical gap, leveraging real-time fileless malware samples. With the available samples, the work enhances the dataset focusing on LOLbins such as dllhost, wscript.exe, etc. A hybrid approach integrating dynamic behaviour and memory forensic artifacts, is the base of this work. It aims to create a dataset that reflects the evolving manoeuvres of fileless malware. With improved accuracy and generalizability, the dataset would be a vital resource for machine learning models and also for the cybersecurity research community. The proposed dataset includes 75 fileless malware samples and 47 benign samples, combined with the existing dataset resulted in a total of 161 samples.

articleTitle: Protection of 3D Models by QIM Watermarking with Reduced Distortion
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This paper explores methods for protecting 3D data stored in the STL format using watermarks. Algorithms based on the QIM family are analyzed as embedding methods. The feasibility of extracting watermarks with absolute accuracy is evaluated, and these methods are compared based on the level of introduced distortions. The evaluation metrics include Mean Squared Error (MSE), the Jaccard index.

articleTitle: Network Intrusion Detection System Based on Multiple Datasets: Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) detect network attacks before they reach host systems. Initially rule-based, NIDS have evolved to leverage machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques. This study evaluates classical ML methods for classifying network attacks across three datasets: HIKARI-2021, UNR-IDD, and CIC-UNSW-NB15. Recursive feature elimination with a Random Forest classifier was employed for feature selection, reducing training and hyperparameter search times. We further implemented a stacking ensemble of tree-based boosting classifiers-XGBoost, LightGBM, and Cat-Boost-for classification. The stacking ensemble achieved the best results, with F1 scores of 93.7% for CIC-UNSW-NB15, 78.1 % for HIKARI-2021, and 95.6% for UNR-IDD. This study highlights the trade-offs between feature selection, model complexity, and dataset size, offering insights into optimizing NIDS performance. The results provide a foundation for future research, particularly on the underexplored UNR-IDD and CIC-UNSW-NB15 datasets.

articleTitle: Quantized Hybrid Privacy Preserving Approach for Federated Learning with Flower Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: The increasing adoption of Decentralized AI systems, especially Federated Learning, has raised significant concerns regarding the privacy and security of sensitive data. These issues can lead to severe financial losses with breaches costing organizations millions annually. To address these issues, this study proposed the Quantized Hybrid Privacy Preserving (QHPP) approach for enhancing data security by maintaining the balance between accuracy, privacy level and efficiency. This novel approach ensures optimal trade-off between accuracy, privacy and efficiency by the unique integration of hybrid techniques with quantization. The study utilized MNIST and Employee Attrition datasets, along with simulation of attacks like label flipping, data poisoning and backdoor attack. Various privacy preserving techniques like Secure Aggregation, Homomorphic Encryption and Differential Privacy along with hybrid approach, combining all the techniques are evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, privacy level, computational and communicational overhead. The results indicate that the hybrid model achieved the highest accuracy of 94.73% across all attacks but suffered from high computational and communicational overhead, highlighting its inefficiency. To address this issue, optimization techniques were evaluated with quantization outperforming other techniques. The proposed QHPP achieved 94.57% accuracy and 0.97 privacy level with significantly lower overhead 1622.11 sec and 6.35 MB on MNIST and 1982 sec and 7.13 MB on Employee Attrition, highlighting its efficiency. Enterprises and Organizations will benefit from the QHPP approach for its efficiency, reduced overhead and enhanced privacy level. The future work will include scalability analysis of QHPP in large-scale FL systems with different datasets and more clients.

articleTitle: Malware Exploitation and Vulnerability Assessment of CVE-2024-38063 in Windows 10 and 11 in Academic Networks Cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This research investigates the vulnerability CVE-2024-38063 in Windows 10 and Windows 11 through detailed experimentation and risk assessment, focusing specifically on the cybersecurity implications for academic network environments. Using a controlled laboratory setup, the study systematically recreated and modified a Proof of Concept (PoC) exploit targeting vulnerabilities in IPv6 fragmentation and HTTP application layers. The testing involved iterative deployments of fragmentation attacks-including overlapping fragments, offset overflow, and reassembly queue flooding-and HTTP service fuzzing, employing tools such as Wireshark and Boofuzz. While direct system compromise was not achieved, the experiments identified significant operational stress, evident from critical CPU usage spikes and poor input validation leading to internal server errors. Additionally, the passive handling of malformed IPv6 packets without explicit logging created critical visibility gaps, indicating potential vulnerabilities for stealthy denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. A structured risk assessment based on the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) and NIST SP 800–53 revealed residual risks even in patched systems, particularly where monitoring and defense mechanisms were inadequate. This study underscores the critical importance of comprehen-sive cybersecurity measures, including continuous vulnerability testing, advanced intrusion detection capabilities, rigorous input validation, and proactive network defense strategies, to effectively mitigate emerging threats in academic settings.

articleTitle: Forensic Investigations in the Age of AI: Identifying and Analyzing Artifacts from AI-Assisted Crimes
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This paper examines the possible manipulation of generative AI models, in particular ChatGPT, to support cybercriminal activities. The research investigates the possibility of coercing AI into assisting malicious actors by setting up a suspect in a cybercrime scenario. In this paper, using a Windows machine and an Android Mobile, we simulate a scenario in which ChatGPT is manipulated to assist a cybercriminal and conduct forensic analysis to reveal evidence of AI involvement. Through integrated memory, mobile, and network forensics, we successfully extract AI-generated artifacts including session tokens, interaction histories, and manipulated prompts that circumvent AI safety measures. Key findings demonstrate how forensic techniques can effectively identify AI involvement in cybercrimes through volatile memory analysis and network traffic examination and how prompt engineering can successfully bypass AI safety measures, exposing vulnerabilities in current safeguards. The paper highlights both opportunities and risks for generative AI in criminal contexts through experimental analysis and forensic techniques. It further discusses ethical and legal issues concerning accountability, misuse of technology, and the potential for harmful behaviors facilitated by AI. These findings demonstrate an imperative need for robust safeguards and specialized forensic approaches to address the exploitation of AI in criminal activities.

articleTitle: A Zero Trust Framework with AI-Driven Identity and Intrusion Detection for Multi-Cloud MLOps
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)

authors.preferredName: H N V Sai Murali Krishna Tungala

abstract: Multi-cloud strategies are transforming enterprise MLOps deployments but introduce security risks such as model poisoning, adversarial inference, and insider threats. Traditional IAM solutions with static policies struggle to protect AI -driven workflows. This paper presents an AI-enhanced Zero Trust Secu-rity (ZTS) framework integrating Federated Identity Management (FIM) and an AI-powered Intrusion Detection System (IDS) to secure multi-cloud MLOps environments. The FIM component is validated using a real-world authentication dataset (LANL), while IDS is tested on intrusion datasets (UNSW-NB15, CIC-IDS2018). The FIM module employs Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models for adaptive authentication. High-risk interactions enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), while low-risk users experience expedited ac-cess. Simultaneously, the AI-driven IDS continuously monitors network traffic and user behavior to detect MLOps-specific threats, including model poisoning and inference API exploitation. Experimental results validate the framework's effectiveness, demonstrating a 38 % reduction in authentication latency, 42 % improvement in threat detection accuracy, and 67 % fewer false positives over baseline methods. The system also scales effectively under increasing user loads. This research highlights the critical role of AI -driven Zero Trust strategies in securing distributed MLOps work-flows, offering a proactive, scalable defense against evolving cyber threats.

articleTitle: Advanced Privacy and Security Techniques in Federated Learning Against Sophisticated Attacks
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This paper addresses the growing vulner-ability of federated learning (FL) systems to sophis-ticated attacks such as model poisoning, Byzantine behavior, and privacy leaks. These threats are critical in sensitive domains (healthcare, finance), where data confidentiality and model integrity are paramount. We propose PRIVFED-AD, a privacy-preserving FL framework integrating adaptive noise injection, ro-bust aggregation, and intelligent attack detection. Our approach dynamically adjusts privacy budgets and employs real-time anomaly detection to mitigate mali-cious activity in large-scale FL deployments. Exper-iments on MNIST, CIFAR-I0, and Healthcare IoT show reductions in attack success rates: 71.7% (model poisoning), 70.6% (Byzantine), 74.7% (reconstruction), and 22.9% (membership inference). Despite height-ened security measures, PRIVFED-AD maintains up to 89.6% accuracy under moderate privacy settings, with robust performance (76.8% accuracy) at 30% malicious clients. We present (1) a unified architecture that balances differential privacy and secure aggre-gation, (2) provable convergence under adversarial conditions, (3) rigorous evaluation across heteroge-neous datasets, and (4) guidelines for large-scale, attack-resilient FL. Compared to existing frameworks, PRIVFED-AD achieves lower attack success rates yet sustains higher accuracy under adversarial settings, establishing a new benchmark for secure FL. Results highlight its potential to secure FL applications and preserve utility, offering a balance between defensive rigor and feasibility.

articleTitle: Customer Personality Analysis Using Machine Learning with Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Predicting customer behavior has become essential for understanding preferences and guiding marketing decisions across various industries. Machine learning and explainable AI (XAI) enable advanced analysis of customer personality traits, facilitating precise segmentation and customized strategies. This study integrates feature engineering, explainability techniques, and state-of-the-art machine learning models to enhance customer personality analysis. Our findings demonstrate that clustering techniques like K-Means significantly improve customer segmentation, while explainability techniques such as SHAP and LIME provide deeper insights into feature importance. Unlike traditional methods, XAI enhances interpretability by offering transparent, actionable insights that marketers can leverage to optimize campaigns and improve customer engagement. Among the various machine learning models evaluated, XGBoost demonstrated the highest performance improvement when applying balancing techniques. Specifically, using Random Oversampling, XGBoost achieved the highest Fl score of 0.8680 compared to other balancing methods. Furthermore, experimental results reveal that incorporating XAI-driven insights leads to a measurable increase in prediction accuracy and segmentation efficiency. The implications of this research extend to decision-making processes in customer-focused organizations, marketing campaign optimization, and customer relationship management. By integrating machine learning, clustering algorithms, and XAI, this study establishes a strong foundation for future customer analysis strategies, paving the way for real-time segmentation and targeted marketing.

articleTitle: Academic Fraud Detection in Online Exams with DNN's Multilayer Model
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This study aims to reveal the best deep learning models that are improved and optimized by predicting undesirable behavior patterns using a dataset consisting of artificial and real exam data of students taking online distance education courses in an online environment through the distance education system. Using online exam data of 129 students, the researchers conducted analysis with two different scenarios to determine the best prediction performance through regression and classification models. The model we proposed was determined as a four-layer DNN with 80.4% test performance in detecting students who “cheated” from undesirable behavior patterns, which was performed with K-10, K-5 and K-3 cross-validation. The results prove that students' online distance education exam data can be easily applied to the DNN model. The models presented in the study provide a roadmap for educational institutions to evaluate their online examination practices and develop more effective strategies for academic honesty.

articleTitle: Remote Laboratory Security Case Study: Physical and Digital Risks of FPGA and Raspberry Pi Farms
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Remote laboratories are crucial platforms for academic research and distributed learning. This paper discusses how remote laboratories controlled by specialized hardware, such as Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and Raspberry Pi farms can present both physical and digital risks. Possible hazards can be caused by a variety of issues, including environmental constraints, hardware degradation, and physical tampering; digitally, the system may suffer from vulnerabilities, such as cyber-attacks, firmware flaws, and network-based intrusions. As such, this paper aims to identify all risk factors while also listing possible mitigation strategies. Ultimately, this study aims to serve as a guide for institutions and organizations in deploying secure and resilient remote laboratory infrastructures.

articleTitle: Enhancing Brain Tumor Detection Using a CNN-Powered Android Application
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Tumors of the brain are a significant clinical prob-lem, which highlights the need for efficient diagnosis at the earliest possible stage to enable effective treatment. Our study explains the development of a brain tumor detection system in real time that is incorporated in an Android application, and it's based on a convolutional neural network (CNN). The suggested system provides a high level of accuracy equal to 99.61%, and can detect four types of brain tumors: gliomas, meningiomas, pituitary tumors, and non-tumorous conditions. Through the use of TensorFlow Lite for mobile deployment, the application guarantees the efficiency of the application as well as working offline, thus making it relevant for real-life use. This study demonstrates that integrating efficient mobile applications with effective deep learning models can help implement real- time brain tumor diagnosis. The results also show how AI-based applications have the possibility of improving brain tumor detection and contributing to early detection.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Secret Sharing using Fully Homomorphic Encryption
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach to improving the security and confidentiality of data exchanged in a network, by combining Shamir's secret sharing and fully homomorphic encryption. This approach is based on the partitioning of infor-mation using Shamir's threshold scheme, enriched by the addition of noise to improve confidentiality. The segments thus created, protected by homomorphic encryption, are sent via distinct paths to an intermediate proxy node capable of directly manipulating the encrypted data and reconstructing the encrypted secret using Lagrange interpolation, then forwarding it to its recipient for de-cryption. Experimental results, obtained on a Windows platform using Python and the NetworkX library, demonstrate that this method not only guarantees data confidentiality and security, but also preserves confidentiality throughout the routing process. This approach represents a significant advance on existing techniques, enhancing data security while maintaining confidentiality at every stage.

articleTitle: Hardware Performance Evaluation of Freeware ETL Tools
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: The extract, transform, load (ETL) process is becoming more important as larger and larger amounts of data are created daily. In this work, ETL software products that can load data, conduct transformations on it, and either save or upload that data to cloud databases were tested. The selected software is either open source or freely available and two datasets have been tested to create aggregated performance evaluations on a local machine. The tested measures are processor use, available memory amount, and committed memory amount. Analysis of the results has determined that Pentaho Kettle and CloverDX are the most hardware-efficient ETL software tested after comparing the results with baseline values of the test computer. Talend Open Studio performed as the least efficient among the tools.

articleTitle: Insider Threat Pattern Detection Using Deep Learning to Evaluate Cyber Value at Risk (CVaR)
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: In an era marked by rapid advancements in information technology, automation has become an integral part of organizational workflows. However, alongside these technological strides, the challenge of data leakage due to insider threats has intensified. Authorized users, while entrusted with privileges, may inadvertently or maliciously compromise sensitive information. Such actions can lead to significant data loss and potentially harm an organization's reputation. In the realm of cybersecurity, insider threats emerge as a formidable adversary. These threats originate from individuals who hold legitimate access to computer networks and systems but exploit their privileges for nefarious purposes. Their actions span a spectrum of malevolence, including IP theft, sabotage, sensitive data exposure, and web application attacks. This paper will discuss the deep learning techniques, which offer a promising avenue for addressing insider threats. It provides an approach to analyze user behavior pattern using rule based deep learning algorithms for identifying abnormal user access to cyber assets indicative of insider threats. Further, the study will discuss the concept of Cyber- Value-at-Risk (CVaR) to quantify the risk due to insider threat originated via various users' activities, accesses, and anomalous behaviors. While study elaborates utilization of deep learning to leverage synthetic data for uncovering hidden patterns and anomalies, it will also discuss the challenges related to dataset availability, privacy, true positives, and false negatives. The fusion of deep learning, insider threat detection, and cyber risk management holds immense potential for safeguarding digital assets and maintaining the integrity of cyberspace. The paper explains limitations and shares future directions for extended research in this context.

articleTitle: Dynamic Threat Detection and Mitigation Using AI-Infused Firewalls
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This research introduces an AI-Infused Firewall that revolutionizes network security by integrating artificial intelligence to detect and mitigate evolving cyber threats. Traditional firewalls often fall short in identifying novel and sophisticated vulnerabilities. Our proposed system addresses this limitation by dynamically adapting firewall rules based on real-time network traffic analysis and employing machine learning for packet classification. Evaluated through performance metrics such as detection accuracy and response time, the system demonstrates efficient threat identification and rapid mitigation. A practical deployment scenario includes securing enterprise networks against zero-day attacks and sophisticated intrusion attempts. Through intelligent automation, the system efficiently detects potential vulnerabilities and mitigates risks by automating security responses, thereby reducing manual intervention. This approach enhances threat detection accuracy, improves overall network security posture, and demonstrates advancements in proactive threat mitigation and efficient network protection.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Classroom Management in Education: Evolution of Academic Studies and Research Trends
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: The transformative effect of technological developments in education has gained momentum with the development of artificial intelligence (AI). The integration of artificial intelligence into education has led to new areas of application, especially in classroom management. Technological developments and AI-supported systems make classroom management more efficient, allowing teachers to analyze student behavior and provide personalized education. Therefore, this study presents a bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence and classroom management. VOSviewer, R studio Bibliometrix package and Gephi application were used for bibliometric analysis. Many analyses were applied on 388 data obtained from the Web of Science (WoS) database. After determining that there were publications between 1991–2025, Lotka's Law was used for author profile and network analysis. After presenting the findings on the most productive sources sub-dimension according to Bradford's Law, the source-author connection was shown with the Three-Field Plot. After the keyword analysis, content-based clustering analysis was performed and relevant articles were grouped into 6 clusters. The main themes related to the field were thus revealed.

articleTitle: An Efficient Plagiarism Detection Algorithm by Ordering Texts of a Document under Scrutiny
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Plagiarism checking is utmost important to find the similarity, authentication and content verification of a document, painting, picture, song, technical drawings, etc. In this paper, we present an efficient textual plagiarism detection algorithm to check the similarity of a document by ordering the texts in the document. In the proposed algorithm, words in the texts of the document are ordered according to the Unicode values. Then, a link to the next word is given after each word by using the memory location of the next word and thus, the ordered document is built. Similarity is sought by comparing each word in the search space with the ordered document. Since the words in a document are ordered, we make use of interpolation search to speed up the search process. The simulation results show that the algorithm can potentially be used for fast plagiarism checking.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Comparative Analysis of RFID Devices Security in Supply Chain Geofencing Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This paper examines RFID technology, dealing with its components, operation, and supply chain applications. A key focus is analyzing cybersecurity vulnerabilities of RFIDs in supply chains. An experiment was conducted to assess these risks, and its methodology and results are presented. Findings highlight security challenges, leading to recommendations for robust RFID deployment in supply chains.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Software Bugs Using Code Context and AST Features
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: A software component plagued with bugs is likely to experience both functional and non-functional difficulties, such as usability, performance, and security issues. These bugs can range from improper layouts to system crashes and security vulnerabilities. In this research, we developed a deep learning-based model to classify software bugs based on preceding and corrected code statements. Preprocessing includes extracting features from the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) by traversing the tree to capture node types and relationships, then encoding the AST into a numerical vector representation for classification. Using AST and padding methods, features are extracted from code statements for use in a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. We proposed a CNN-based model with AST-based feature extraction for large-scale software bug classification and evaluated on 153,652 bug samples from 1,000 GitHub projects. Compared to traditional datasets, this large dataset presents challenges in building accurate prediction models. This model is particularly useful in continuous integration (CI) pipelines, where it can automatically detect problematic code during the build process, helping to identify bugs faster and reduce manual review.

articleTitle: Enhancing Phishing Website Detection with Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This paper examines the impact of feature selection on phishing website detection using machine learning techniques. We utilize the UCI Phishing Website dataset, which consists of 11,055 instances and 30 features with no missing values. Our results show that the random forest outperforms logistic regression, achieving an accuracy of 97.11%. By analyzing feature importance, we optimize the model by removing detrimental features, further improving accuracy to 97.74%. This study highlights the effectiveness of the random forest in phishing detection and underscores the importance of feature selection in enhancing model performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing loMT Security with Deep Learning Based Approach for Medical IoT Threat Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: The rapid spread of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) systems makes the security of these systems critical. Although IoMT can improve patient care and optimize health care services, it also poses cyberattacks and data breaches. In this context, securing IoMT systems is important for patient privacy and system integrity. A deep learning-based approach is proposed in this study to detect cyberattacks that may occur in IoMT systems. Deep Neural Networks (DNN) and Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) architectures are used on the CICIoMT2024 dataset. An Fl-score of 99% was achieved for binary classification and over 75% for categorical and multiclass classification tasks. In particular, the LSTM architecture exhibited high performance in detecting complex attack patterns. The experimental results provide new insights for future research and provide effective and scalable solutions to improve the security of IoMT systems.

articleTitle: A Multi-Layer Model of Psychological Factors and Parametric Approaches for Human-Centric Phishing Prevention
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Phishing continues to be an evolving cybersecurity menace, leveraging social engineering that preys on human vulnerabilities, such as risk-taking, trust, and cognitive biases. This research aims to systematically model these psychological dimensions using a six-category hierarchical framework Demographic Factors (DF), Digital Literacy (DL), Risk-Taking Behavior (RTB), Trust Perception (TP), Psychological State (PS), and Cognitive Bias (CB) quantified by standardized scales (e.g., DOSPERT, Karolinska Sleepiness Scale). We integrate these factors via either a Hooking Factor (HF) domain-based formula or Logistic Regression (LR), applying SMOTE to mitigate class imbalance in our limited dataset (126 participants, only 8 actual phishing victims). A comparative analysis with existing phishing detection approaches highlights our psychological emphasis and flexible modeling strategy. Our key findings demonstrate: (1) Both HF and LR yield interpretable insights into user-level phishing vulnerability; (2) SMOTE helps minority-class recognition but may inflate performance; and (3) future real-time biometric monitoring of stress or fatigue could boost the model's adaptive capacity. We contribute a human-centric perspective that merges psychological measurement with machine learning for enhanced phishing defense strategies.

articleTitle: Comparing Traditional Hacking Tools and AI-Driven Alternatives
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Traditional hacking tools continue to evolve, providing hackers with powerful means to exploit vulnerabilities, which increases the demand for effective countermeasures by cybersecurity specialists. These tools, while often associated with malicious use, are also essential for legitimate activities like Penetration Testing or Vulnerability Assessment. New simulator and emulator tools combine the functionality of previous existing tools into an all-in-one integrated solution, like the MITRE Caldera emulator platform and the Cyberwheel simulator. These platforms have been enhanced with new AI agents in the decision-making process allowing the autonomous execution of defensive and offensive actions according to a specific attack type which is the case of Cyberwheel. We compare the features of these three tool categories, traditional Hacking tools, all-in-one tools such as MITRE Caldera, and AI-driven tools such as the Cyberwheel simulator, in terms of attack actions supported, integration of different techniques and the advantage of using AI. We conclude that all-in-one solutions are a good starting point to explore developments in AI -driven defensive and offensive actions. In particular, the Cyberwheel simulator proved the feasibility of using AI -driven agents to perform defensive and offensive actions according to the MITRE ATT &CK Framework.

articleTitle: Evaluating Spam Detection Techniques: A Comparison of TF-IDF and Sentence Embeddings with Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of spam detection models using two feature extraction techniques: TF-IDF and Sentence Embeddings. The study evaluates three machine learning models: Random Forest, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression, to classify spam messages. Optuna, a hyperparameter optimization framework, is applied to tune Random Forest and XGBoost classifiers. Results are compared in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, fl-score, support, execution time, train time and tune time.

articleTitle: Extent of an Attack in an Attack Graph: Method to Evaluate Evidence Set
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Evaluating the impact of an attack in a system is essential for prioritizing response towards simultaneous threats. While some attacks will impact lower-valued resources of the system, whereas other attacks have an impact on disrupting critical components. A quantifiable metric for impact would serve as a valuable tool to prioritize attack scenarios based on their potential damage. Our study proposes a structural approach to measure the severity of an attack by integrating a vulnerability assessment framework that includes the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) score, the Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) score, along with economic factors.

articleTitle: PowerShell Proxy-Aware Intercommunication and Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: With the exponential expansion of attacks, organizations and enterprises nowadays, force their network communication through a proxy. This measure can assist security analysts to better control their environment, and monitor traffic. Likewise, attackers are interested in the manipulation techniques of the proxy concept, since they are aware of this protection. On the other hand, penetration testers (also known as, ethical attackers, or hackers) must ensure that their techniques (while generating payloads) can work through proxy to understand better steps that need to be mitigated. Additionally, they can always attempt to manipulate the proxy if possible [1], [2], along with any of its implemented monitors for this purpose. Usually, the PowerShell download cradles may not always be proxy-aware. However, the Meterpreter HTTP and HTTPS are [3]. A Meterpreter is a Metasploit attack payload that provides an interactive shell from which an attacker can proceed with his exploration of the target machine and run codes. Our focus will be based on strategies to talk to a proxy, i.e., we will need to use some modules which by default, are proxy-aware in the creation of our payloads [4]. We may still face some issues with some classes that are proxy-aware, since they may be reverted in future versions of Windows.

articleTitle: Enhancing Trust and Security in Learning Management Systems: Addressing Submission Concerns with Timestamp Transparency and Digital Signatures
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Learning Management Systems (LMS) are indis-pensable tools in modern education, enabling streamlined interaction between educators and learners. However, for these systems to be effective, they must be both secure and trustworthy. While often conflated, security and trust represent distinct components. Security pertains to the technical safeguards protecting data integrity and confidentiality, whereas trust involves the users' perception of the system's reliability and fairness. Our experi-ence highlights two recurring concerns among students when submitting assignments via an LMS: (1) ambiguity regarding how submission timestamps are determined, and (2) uncertainty about whether their submission has been successfully received and is tamper-proof. To address the first issue, we propose that LMS platforms prominently display the system's official timestamp to the user at the moment of submission. This measure ensures that students are aware of the time standard governing deadlines and mitigates disputes over late submissions. To resolve the second concern, we introduce a robust digital signature mechanism. Upon submission, the LMS digitally signs the file using cryptographic techniques, generating a verifiable receipt that is securely distributed to both the student and the instructor. This approach provides dual benefits: students gain assurance that their work has been successfully submitted and acknowledged, while instructors can verify the integrity of the submission, ensuring that no modifications occur post-delivery. This dual-layer solution enhances trust in LMS platforms by addressing key user concerns while upholding rigorous security standards. Our framework lays the foundation for further re-search into the intersection of security, trust, and user experience in diaital learning environments.

articleTitle: The Role of Machine Learning in Distance Education
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This study aims to present a bibliometric analysis to examine the role of machine learning in distance education. The analysis of 1768 articles obtained from the Web of Science database between 2005 and 2024, using the keywords “machine learning, deep learning, distance education, e-Iearning, and online learning,” was conducted using the Biblioshiny software. The analytical approach used in this study covers a range of bibliometric indicators, including keywords, authors, documents, sources, and countries. A significant increase in the number of publications on the topic has been observed since 2017. The majority of the studies come from China and the United States, which are also the countries with the highest number of citations. Nanyang Technological University and Tsinghua University are among the institutions with the highest number of publications on the topic. IEEE Access, Education and Information Technologies, and Applied Sciences-Basel are the journals where the articles are most frequently published. “Online learning,” “machine learning,” and “deep learning” are the most frequently used keywords. This study highlights the increasing importance of machine learning in distance education and provides valuable insights for future research.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Deep Learning for Energy Time Series Forecasting: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Deep learning methods have achieved widespread success and are continually being utilized in new domains, including the prediction of energy time series. However, these methods do not indicate their confidence in predictions, hindering the ability to evaluate, interpret, and enhance forecast accuracy. As a result, this research delves into the exploration of probabilistic extensions to deep learning and their implementation in energy time series forecasting. The evaluated methods include concrete dropout, deep ensembles, Bayesian neural networks, deep Gaussian processes, and functional neural processes. Two load forecasting scenarios are considered for evaluation: short-term (single-step) and day-ahead (multi-step) forecasting. The methods are assessed based on calibration, sharpness, and proficiency in indicating a lack of knowledge. To provide a reference, a simple neural network and a quantile regression model are also employed. Overall, the methods demonstrate strong performance, with concrete dropout, deep ensembles, and Bayesian neural networks performing equally well or better than the reference methods. Functional neural processes and deep Gaussian processes exhibit weaker performance, likely attributed to convergence issues and suboptimal parameters. Notably, deep ensembles prove to be straightforward to implement and train, requiring very few hyperparameters.

articleTitle: IoT Cyberattack Detection via Fog Computing and Multilayer Perceptron Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel methodology designed for detecting cyberattacks in Internet of Things (IoT) fog computing scenarios through the application of a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) neural network trained and validated on custom-generated datasets. Network traffic was captured under strictly controlled conditions using resource-constrained edge devices, such as the Raspberry Pi 4 and Jetson Nano, ensuring realistic and representative IoT interactions. Traffic scenarios include typical benign activities such as automated web browsing and standard DNS lookups, as well as targeted Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks designed to saturate device resources and disrupt normal operations. The captured data underwent structured processing and feature extraction using Zeek, an open-source network traffic analyzer aligned precisely with the established NF-ToN-IoT dataset feature set. The MLP model trained showed exceptional performance, achieving near-perfect metrics for Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score. To validate the robustness and generalization capabilities further, external evaluations were performed using datasets consisting exclusively of unseen malicious and benign network flows. These external validations confirmed the model's ability to accurately identify previously unencountered attack patterns and reliably distinguish benign interactions, under-scoring its effectiveness and practical viability for enhancing cybersecurity in IoT fog computing deployment.

articleTitle: Assessing the Usability of an AI-Powered Mobile App on Student Engagement in Remote Field Activities
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This mixed research study aimed to use a mobile app ‘Neo-Light’ by university students in remote field study locations to eliminate the limitation of carrying traditional hard-copy maps in remote field studies. The study is specific to determining whether mobile app can effectively replace hard-copy maps to conduct field studies. The study's primary objective was to examine the role of mobile learning in supporting university students with their geospatial field activities such that reliance on traditional hard copy maps can be reduced and a more interactive basis for learning using digital mapping tools employed. The specific issue that the authors addressed was to replace traditional modes of learning, which used obsolete approaches for landscape interpretation using paper maps, leading to pedagogically inflexible and disconnected curriculum design for contemporary students. The study employs a usability testing methodology based on the ISO 9241–11 standard to measure usability factors (effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction) to assist future researchers in identifying emerging mobile learning practices in higher education. This study discovered that mobile learning was associated with a positive influence on students' geospatial knowledge, yielding 93% competence when completing mapping activities. With increasing educational applications, a better user experience is essential. Higher education institutions are responsible for providing accessible student infrastructure and should emphasize interactions that foster significant changes in an information and communication-based society.

articleTitle: Illuminated Secrets: Exploiting Display Brightness for Out-of-Band Optical Covert Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: In recent years, covert communication techniques have gained increased attention due to their potential to bypass traditional security measures. While many existing methods have focused on network-based exfiltration, this paper explores a novel approach that leverages a device's display brightness as an out-of-band optical covert communication channel. By utilizing native system tools such as PowerShell and Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI), we demonstrate how brightness modulation can be exploited to covertly transmit data. This method mimics common visual anomalies, such as screen flickering or cable malfunctions, allowing the data transmission to go unnoticed. Unlike traditional approaches, our technique requires no external plugins or libraries, making it highly adaptable and difficult to detect. Experimental results demonstrate its effectiveness in real-world scenarios, highlighting the method's potential.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Supervised Learning Models on Distinct Datasets for Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Malware detection remains a critical challenge as cybersecurity threats continue to evolve, particularly with the rise of memory-resident and mobile malware. In this study, we evaluate the performance of three supervised learning models-Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Decision Tree-across two distinct datasets: CIC-MaIMem-2022 (focused on memory-resident malware) and CIC-MaIDroid-2020 (targeting Android malware). Our findings show that while all models perform exceptionally well on memory-based malware, Random Forest achieves the highest accuracy for mobile malware classification, highlighting its ability to handle complex patterns. Additionally, hyperparameter tuning further improves model robustness, demonstrating the impact of optimization in challenging detection scenarios. This study provides insights into the strengths and limitations of different models, contributing to more effective machine learning-based malware detection strategies.

articleTitle: Cost-Optimized Cloud Scheduling for ETL and Big Data Using AI
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Cloud-based data pipelines are critical for large-scale ETL and big data analytics, yet in-efficient scheduling leads to high costs and resource underutilization. Traditional approaches, such as static provisioning and rule-based auto-scaling, fail to adapt to dynamic workloads and ever-changing cloud pricing. This paper introduces an AI-driven cost-aware scheduling framework that integrates LSTM-based workload forecasting, Isolation Forest anomaly detection, and real-time cost analytics. Unlike purely reactive or threshold-based methods, this approach proactively adjusts resources to minimize costs and prevent performance bottlenecks. Experiments using the Google Cluster Workload Traces dataset and Azure VM Pricing data demonstrate up to a 30-40% reduction in operational expenses, along with improved processing efficiency and auto-scaling responsiveness. However, the proposed solution may require further adaptation for extreme-scale scenarios or specialized compliance environments. These findings highlight the novelty of combining predictive analytics, anomaly detection, and cost optimization, offering a robust strategy for enhancing performance and reducing expenses in cloud-based ETL and big data workflows.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Models for Malware Family Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Malware attacks have been rising, and the response for detection and mitigation have fallen short to counter the threats. The advances in artificial intelligence have not yielded a comprehensive solution in early detection of mal ware and its variants, making this a critical gap. Our work leverages on the biology-inspired analysis of malware trace sequences and clustering based on trace similarity computation. The malware traces extracted from the community detection algorithms are assumed to represent malware families precisely. The deep learning framework uses the most prototypical features from the extracted traces for prediction of mal ware families. In this work, deep learning models in the form of artificial neural networks (ANNs) are evaluated and experimental results are presented. The results elucidate the deep learning framework for malware family detection across different variations of detection and training splits.

articleTitle: DockerGate: Automated Seccomp Policy Generation for Docker Images
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: With Docker's rising adoption in cloud services, security concerns arise due to its default access to extensive system calls, increasing the host kernel's attack surface. Docker's Seccomp profiles offer a way to restrict system calls but require intricate, image-specific configurations. I introduce DockerGate, a tool for automated Seccomp policy generation tailored to Docker images. DockerGate employs static analysis to map and aggregate the necessary system calls from binaries within a container image, generating minimal privilege profiles. my methodology involves analyzing ELF binaries using tools like nm, 1dd, and objdump to identify system calls invoked by dynamically linked libraries. Testing DockerGate on 110 Docker images demonstrates its effectiveness in reducing system call access while maintaining container functionality, significantly narrowing the attack surface and enhancing security in containerized environments.

articleTitle: The Relationship Between Secondary School Students' Digital Game Addictions and Their Responsibilities Toward Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: This study aimed to examine the relationship between secondary school students' digital game addiction and their responsibility levels toward learning. The sample of the study consisted of 369 eighth-grade students enrolled during the 2024–2025 academic year. In data collection, scales to measure digital game addiction and responsibility toward learning for children were used. The study was conducted using a correlational survey model. It was concluded that the average levels of digital game addiction were at a risky level. It was also found that digital game addiction differed statistically based on the gender variable, with boys being more addicted to digital games. The average levels of responsibility toward learning were found to be high. Furthermore, it was concluded that responsibility toward learning did not differ statistically in a significant way based on the gender variable. A negative and moderate statistically significant relationship was found between digital game addiction and responsibility toward learning. As middle school students' digital game addiction increases, their responsibility toward learning decreases. In addition, it was determined that digital game addiction has a predictive effect on responsibility toward learning.

articleTitle: Thermographic Detection of Tool Wear: A Review on Deep Learning-Based Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: In machining processes, cutting tool wear is a critical problem affecting key performance parameters such as surface quality, production time, and cost. High temperatures cause deformation and wear in the tool material and shorten tool life. This reduces production efficiency and negatively affects the sustainability of quality-oriented goals such as zerodefect manufacturing. In this review study, the current literature on the prediction of cutting tool wear in machining processes using thermal imaging and deep learning techniques is analyzed. With advancing manufacturing technologies, unattended machining capability and the proliferation of approaches such as Zero Defect Manufacturing (ZDM), realtime and accurate monitoring of cutting tool conditions is a strategic requirement for production efficiency and quality control. In this context, the possibilities offered by indirect wear detection methods based on temperature data and the applications of deep learning-based models in this field are evaluated. Significant success has been achieved in tool life prediction by processing temperature maps obtained with thermal cameras, thermocouples, and infrared (IR) imaging systems using algorithms such as CNN and ANN. The methods in the literature are discussed comparatively and their advantages and limitations are discussed. This paper systematically reviews the existing approaches in the literature for tool wear monitoring using temperature-based methods and provides a comprehensive review for future research in this area.

articleTitle: Enhancing Kalman Filter Resilience in Electric Vehicles: Cyber-Attack Mitigation with Machine Learning Based Adaptive Filtering
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) depend on Kalman Filters for precision in navigation and control; however, these systems can be exposed to cyber-attacks such as Denial-of-Service (DoS) and data injections, which can compromise sensor data integrity. This study presents a unique approach that combines Adaptive Kalman Filters with Isolation Forest algorithm to detect real-time anomaly and adjust the parameters to improve system resilience. Simulation-based experiments were conducted, demonstrating that the Adaptive Kalman Filter can reduce the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) by 40% and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 35% during cyber-attacks compared to Standard Kalman Filters. The findings from this study illustrate that implementing both Adaptive Kalman Filters with machine learning-based anomaly detection methods can significantly improve the cyber resilience of electric vehicles and strengthen the development of a stronger state estimation framework, improving the cybersecurity and reliability of EV sensor fusion systems.

articleTitle: Human-in-the-Loop: Legal Knowledge Formalization in Attempto Controlled English
publicationTitle: 2025 13th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: Automating legal knowledge through the use of computational languages presents a series of challenges, particularly in translating complex normative texts into formalized representations that are semantically faithful and computationally valid. A salient concern is reconciling the ambiguity inherent in natural legal language with the syntactic constraints of controlled languages.
